To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and synthesized a new polyurea chemistry that enables facile and tunable bulk cross-linking of shape memory polymeric systems by electron beam irradiations.

we have developed a new polyurethanes chemistry that enables the tunable bulk cross-linking of thermoplastic shape-memory polymer systems by electron beam irradiations without the use of radiation-sensitization additives.
the incorporation of a structural motif into the side chain of a thermoplastic poly(ester-urethane) polymer enables facile bulk electron beam cross-linkability without sensitizing additives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new platform chemistry for the design and fabrication of thermally stable, bulk cross-linkable, shape memory polymers.
the development of a new, tunable polyurethane SMP chemistry that enables bulk cross-linking of highly processable thermoplastics by e-beam irradiation.

developing and implementing a platform chemistry that enables the bulk electron beam cross-linkable, low-molecule weight thermoplastics that are required to enable the high-throughput thermomechanical processing of SMP materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incorporation of a novel structural motif into the thermoplatcic polymer side chain enabled the bulk cross-linking of a thermoplastic SMP system without the need for radiation-sensitizers, which is an important step towards enabling the practical use of these materials in high throughput processing applications.

the incorporation of specific structural motifs into low-molecular weight, aliphatic thermoplastics has enabled the development of an entirely new polyurethane SMP platform that is capable of being processed at high throughput and is tunable in its thermomechanical behavior by bulk electron beam cross-linkage.
this work provides a platform chemistry for the development of a new class of thermally processable, electron-beam cross-linkable, and tunable thermomechanical polyurethane SMP systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that it is possible to establish an electron beam cross-linkable, thermally stable polyurethane chemistry with tunable bulk cross-link density and mechanical properties, which is an important step toward developing a platform chemistry for the fabrication of SMPs by electron beam cross-linkage.

a novel polyurethane chemistry has been established to enable the tunable, bulk cross-linking of thermoplastics by e-beam irradiation and that the thermomechanical behavior of these new materials has been characterized and correlated to their chemical structures.
we have established a platform chemistry that enables facile cross-linking of thermoplastics by e-beam, which has the potential to significantly impact the design of shape memory polymer systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of structural motifs into the side chains of thermoplastic polyols that are capable of undergoing electron beam cross-linkage can be used to establish a platform chemistry that enables the facile and bulk cross-linking of shape memory polymeric systems.

the incorporation of specific structural motifs in the polymer side chain of a thermoplastic SMP can enable the bulk, electron beam cross-linkable thermomechanical tunability that is characteristic of traditional thermoset SMPs, but without the practical processing limitations and thermal instability of radiation sensitizers.
the incorporation of a structural motif into a thermoplastic polymer can enable the bulk, tunable, and radiation-sensitizer free cross-linking of thermoplastic SMPs.
